$schema_note: AUTHORED, and deliberately small. It carries the Thompson plat's BLOCK NUMBERS for the blocks this reconstruction can reach them, and the numbering scheme inside a block, with the reading each rests on. Read by tools/generate_plat_lots.py, which stamps `plat_block_number` onto a block of data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json and `plat_lot_number` onto its lots. Nothing here authors geometry: a block's boundary and its lot lines are derived from the committed street lines exactly as before, and this file only puts a NUMBER on them.
why_this_file_exists: The most precise placement statement in the whole newspaper corpus is G. Spring's For-Sale notice — 'LOT No. 7, in block No. 16, one lot east of Haddock's Tavern, on Lake street' — and it resolved to nothing, because data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json keys its blocks on their bounding streets and no committed source numbered one. Three separate readings recorded that the address was the most placeable thing the corpus said and that placing it was somebody else's job (T-0324, and the June and October readings of the notice). This file is that job. T-0358.
grades: Each entry's `confidence` grades THE NUMBER ON THIS BLOCK, not the block. Nothing here is `documented`: the two numerals that are read off a survey sheet are read at this dataset's own ±20 m georeference, so even they carry an identification step that a sheet does not make for us. `numeral_on_sheet` says which two those are, so the difference between a numeral that was read and a numeral that was counted does not vanish into one grade.

reading.asset_note: The project owner's crop of Wright's 1834 survey sheet at the Clark reach, supplied 2026-08-13. 639 × 719 px. Unlike the rest of that directory it is a piece of the master survey, so the ordinary Wright rules apply and it may drive geometry.
reading.what_it_carries: TWO adjacent blocks in one tier, the western numbered 19 and the eastern 18, separated by a street with the platted 80 written in it, and a narrow sinuous watercourse drawn down that street. Block 18's north row of lots is numbered 4 3 2 running west to east and its south row 5 6 7 running west to east; the fourth lot of each row falls outside the crop.
reading.correction: docs/RESEARCH/clark_reach_bulge_1834.md § 8 and docs/RESEARCH/thompson_plat_grid.md § 4 both said this crop reads 'block numbers 19, 18 and 17'. Re-read at full resolution on 2026-08-29 it carries 19 and 18 and no 17 — the map region ends at the east edge of block 18. Two consecutive numerals still fix the step and the direction, which is all either memo used the third for, but the evidence base is two blocks and both memos now say two.
reading.direction: The number falls by one for each block eastward along a tier, so it rises westward. That the run is along the TIER and not down a column follows from the two numerals being side by side in one row and one apart: a column-major numbering would separate two blocks in the same row by the number of rows.

identification.method: the watercourse in the street between the two blocks, which this project has already traced and committed
identification.note: docs/RESEARCH/clark_reach_bulge_1834.md § 4 measured the drawn watercourse's mouth at local E +462…+469 and established that the committed trace runs up the inside of its own ink line there — the stream is real, traced, and NOT the river bulge that memo was about. That places the street the stream runs down in the east half of the La Salle corridor. The nearest alternatives are Wells at E +329.3 (122 m west) and Clark at E +574.7 (123 m east), so the identification is unambiguous at this dataset's ±20 m working uncertainty even though it is an inference. The two blocks the crop numbers are therefore the Wells–La Salle block (19) and the La Salle–Clark block (18) of the tier fronting South Water Street on the north and Lake Street on the south.

lot_numbering.scheme: counter-clockwise from the block's north-east corner: lot 1 at the east end of the north row, running WEST to lot 4 at its west end; lot 5 at the west end of the south row, running EAST to lot 8 at its east end.
lot_numbering.read_from: block 18, whose north row the crop sets 4 3 2 west to east and whose south row it sets 5 6 7 west to east. Lots 1 and 8 fall outside the crop and complete the run.
lot_numbering.note: THE SCHEME IS READ ON ONE BLOCK AND THE LINES IT NUMBERS ARE NOT DRAWN FROM ANY SHEET. Four lots to a block face is itself a reading of this same block (docs/RESEARCH/thompson_plat_grid.md § 4) and the lot lines in data/traces/vectors/thompson_lots.json are the module divided into a block, graded `conjectural` for that reason. A number put on a conjectural line is conjectural whatever the number's own provenance, so every emitted `plat_lot_number` carries this grade — including block 18's own, where the numerals are the ones the crop shows. What the scheme is good for is reading a documented ADDRESS onto the grid, which is what it was fetched for, and not for asserting where a lot line ran.
lot_numbering.emitted_for: only the blocks numbered below. A lot number without a block number says nothing.

blocks.note: Two blocks west of the read 19, counted at one block per step along the tier. THE BLOCK NOW BUILDS: it was OMITTED from the generated grid until 2026-08-30, because South Water Street's committed centreline stopped 24 m short of it, and T-0183 closed that street's west end on Market's corridor (docs/RESEARCH/thompson_plat_grid.md § 6.2), so the number is stamped onto a block rather than onto an omission. Nothing says whether the tier's run continues west of Market Street; only that this block is two steps from one that was read.
One block west of the read 19, counted at one block per step along the tier. No independent statement corroborates this number.

THE NUMERAL IS READ OFF THE SHEET; WHICH BLOCK CARRIES IT IS INFERRED. The crop sets 19 on the western of its two blocks, and the watercourse drawn in the street between them is the one this project traced at local E +462…+469, which is the La Salle corridor — so the block west of it is the Wells–La Salle block. The grade is the weaker of the two steps.

THE NUMERAL IS READ OFF THE SHEET; WHICH BLOCK CARRIES IT IS INFERRED, by the same watercourse. This is also the block whose lot numbering the crop shows, and the block from which four-lots-to-a-face was read in the first place — so it is the one block here where the plat grid's subdivision and its numbering rest on the same reading.

Two blocks east of the read 19, counted at one block per step along the tier. No independent statement corroborates this number. Both memos that previously claimed the crop READ a 17 were describing this block; it is counted, not read.

THREE BLOCKS EAST OF THE READ 19 — AND THE ONE DERIVED NUMBER HERE THAT AN INDEPENDENT SOURCE AGREES WITH. G. Spring's For-Sale notice puts 'LOT No. 7, in block No. 16' ON LAKE STREET and 'one lot east of Haddock's Tavern' (Chicago Democrat, 1834-06-18 c006; also 1834-09-03 c005, 1834-10-15 c006, 1834-11-19 c010). Counting east gives block 16 the Dearborn–State block of the South Water tier, whose Lake Street frontage is its south row — and under the lot scheme above the south row runs 5 6 7 8 west to east from the Dearborn corner, so lot 7 is the THIRD lot east of Dearborn and Haddock's Tavern, one lot west of it, is the SECOND. That is where this dataset already stands the Mansion House, which is Haddock's Tavern: Andreas has it 'on Lake near Dearborn', and T-0324 read J. K. Botsford's advertisements — 'next door to Graves' Tavern' and 'Corner of Dearborn and Lake-sts.' — as one frontage on the corner lot, which puts the tavern on the second lot from Dearborn (docs/RESEARCH/botsford_graves_1834.md). The count, the newspaper's own 'on Lake street', and a placement argued from Andreas and Botsford before this file existed all land on the same block face. The arithmetic is still arithmetic and the grade stays `inferred`; what the agreement buys is that three statements made independently do not contradict it.

refused.scope: every block of the Lake–Randolph and Randolph–Washington tiers (14 held by this reconstruction)
refused.reason: The crop fixes the direction of the run WITHIN a tier and says nothing whatever about how it passes from one tier to the next. A boustrophedon that turns back west, a run that restarts at the west end of each tier, and a run that descends a column all reproduce 19 beside 18 and give these blocks different numbers. No committed source chooses between them, so they are refused rather than counted.

refused.scope: blk_south_water_clinton, blk_lake_clinton, blk_randolph_clinton and every other West Division block
refused.reason: West of the South Branch, and nothing read here says whether the South Division's run continues across the river, restarts, or belongs to a separate numbering altogether.
Not in the grid at all — its street control is what ROADMAP § S9 still records as owed, so there are no blocks to number.

refused.scope: where the tier's run begins and ends
refused.reason: Only offsets from the two read numerals are claimed. Whether 21 is the westernmost number of this tier, and whether 16 is its easternmost, is not established by anything here; State Street is the platted town's eastern edge and Market Street's block is the last one east of the South Branch, but a plat may number past a boundary this project has not read.

None was consulted and none may be. The numbers here are counted from two numerals on a committed survey sheet and from nothing else; if a reprint agrees, that is a corroboration somebody may fetch and cite, and if it disagrees it is evidence, but neither may be substituted for this reading without saying so.
